greek: Ταῦτα τὰ ὀνόματα τῶν υἱῶν Ισραηλ τῶν εἰσπεπορευμένων εἰς Αἴγυπτον ἅμα Ιακωβ τῷ πατρὶ αὐτῶν — ἕκαστος πανοικίᾳ αὐτῶν εἰσήλθοσαν —·
hint: The names of Israel's sons who went into Egypt with Jacob, each with his household.

notes.text: With Jacob their father: the Hebrew has ʾēt yaʿăqōb, with Jacob, without their father.
Perfect participle of εἰσπορεύομαι: the ones who have entered, and are there.

Not in Middle Liddell; LSJ gives πανοικία, whole household, and the dative as an adverb, with all the house, the dative's own English and so not marked again. The nominative of GEN 50:8 has the first alone.

names.gloss: (Ισραηλ, from Hebrew Yiśrāʾēl, which the Hebrew of Genesis 32:29 hears in śārâ ʿim ʾĕlōhîm, "he strove with God")
(Αἴγυπτος, the Greek name of the land; Hebrew Miṣrayim)
(Ιακωβ, from Hebrew Yaʿăqōb, which the Hebrew of Genesis 25:26 hears in ʿāqēb, "heel")

greek: Ρουβην, Συμεων, Λευι, Ιουδας,
hint: The list of Jacob's sons begins: Reuben, Simeon, Levi, Judah.

notes.text: Leah's first four sons, in the order of their births at Genesis 29:32–35.

names.gloss: (Ρουβην, from Hebrew Rĕʾûbēn, which the Hebrew of Genesis 29:32 hears in rāʾâ bĕʿonyî, "he has seen my affliction")
(Συμεων, from Hebrew Šimʿôn, which the Hebrew of Genesis 29:33 hears in šāmaʿ, "he heard")
(Λευι, from Hebrew Lēwî, which the Hebrew of Genesis 29:34 hears in lāwâ, "he was joined")
(Ιουδας, from Hebrew Yĕhûdâ, which the Hebrew of Genesis 29:35 hears in yādâ, "to praise")

greek: Ισσαχαρ, Ζαβουλων καὶ Βενιαμιν,
hint: The list goes on with Issachar, Zebulun and Benjamin.

notes.text: Leah's last two sons, then Rachel's younger; Joseph, her elder, is named apart in 1:5.

reading: [[name:Ισσαχαρ]], [[name:Ζαβουλων]] and [[name:Βενιαμιν]],

names.gloss: (Ισσαχαρ, from Hebrew Yiśśāśkār, which the Hebrew of Genesis 30:18 hears in śākār, "wages")
(Ζαβουλων, from Hebrew Zĕbûlûn, which the Hebrew of Genesis 30:20 hears in zābal, "to dwell with honour")
(Βενιαμιν, from Hebrew Binyāmîn, "son of the right hand" or "son of the south")

greek: Δαν καὶ Νεφθαλι, Γαδ καὶ Ασηρ.
hint: The list ends with the four sons of the maidservants: Dan, Naphtali, Gad and Asher.

notes.text: Bilhah's sons, then Zilpah's, as at Genesis 35:25–26.

reading: [[name:Δαν]] and [[name:Νεφθαλι]], [[name:Γαδ]] and [[name:Ασηρ]].

names.gloss: (Δαν, from Hebrew Dān, which the Hebrew of Genesis 30:6 hears in dîn, "he judged")
(Νεφθαλι, from Hebrew Naptālî, which the Hebrew of Genesis 30:8 hears in niptal, "I have wrestled")
(Γαδ, from Hebrew Gād, which the Hebrew of Genesis 30:11 hears in gād, "fortune")
(Ασηρ, from Hebrew ʾĀšēr, which the Hebrew of Genesis 30:13 hears in ʾōšer, "happiness")

greek: Ιωσηφ δὲ ἦν ἐν Αἰγύπτῳ. ἦσαν δὲ πᾶσαι ψυχαὶ ἐξ Ιακωβ πέντε καὶ ἑβδομήκοντα.
hint: Joseph was already in Egypt; Jacob's descendants number seventy-five, where the Hebrew counts seventy.

notes.text: Seventy-five, as at Genesis 46:27 in this Greek; the Hebrew has šibʿîm, seventy. Stephen's speech, Acts 7:14, gives seventy-five.
The Greek puts Joseph first; the Hebrew counts the souls first and ends with Joseph.
From Jacob: the Hebrew has yōṣĕʾê yerek yaʿăqōb, coming out of Jacob's thigh.

greek: καθότι δὲ αὐτοὺς ἐταπείνουν, τοσούτῳ πλείους ἐγίνοντο καὶ ἴσχυον σφόδρα σφόδρα· καὶ ἐβδελύσσοντο οἱ Αἰγύπτιοι ἀπὸ τῶν υἱῶν Ισραηλ.
hint: The more the Egyptians oppress them, the more they multiply, and the Egyptians come to loathe them.

notes.text: In what measure … by so much: τοσοῦτος in the dative with a comparative, the measure of the difference.
And they grew very very strong: not in the Hebrew, which has kēn yirbeh wĕkēn yip̄rōṣ, so they multiplied and so they spread.
βδελύσσομαι, to feel nausea, to loathe: for the Hebrew wayyāquṣû, they felt dread.

greek: Καὶ εἶπεν ὁ βασιλεὺς τῶν Αἰγυπτίων ταῖς μαίαις τῶν Εβραίων, τῇ μιᾷ αὐτῶν, ᾗ ὄνομα Σεπφωρα, καὶ τὸ ὄνομα τῆς δευτέρας Φουα,
hint: The king of Egypt speaks to the Hebrews' midwives, Shiphrah and Puah.

notes.text: The midwives of the Hebrews: the genitive leaves open whether they were Hebrew themselves, as the Hebrew hamĕyalĕdōt hāʿibriyyōt does.
Middle Liddell's first sense is good mother, dame, a term of address for an old woman; midwife is its last.

names.gloss: (Εβραῖος, from Hebrew ʿIbrî, usually connected with ʿēber, "the region beyond")
(Σεπφωρα, from Hebrew Šiprâ, usually connected with šāpar, "to be fair")
(Φουα, from Hebrew Pûʿâ, of uncertain meaning)

greek: καὶ εἶπεν Ὅταν μαιοῦσθε τὰς Εβραίας καὶ ὦσιν πρὸς τῷ τίκτειν, ἐὰν μὲν ἄρσεν ᾖ, ἀποκτείνατε αὐτό, ἐὰν δὲ θῆλυ, περιποιεῖσθε αὐτό.
hint: He orders them to kill the Hebrew women's sons at birth and let the daughters live.

notes.text: And they are near the bearing: the Hebrew has ûrĕʾîten ʿal-hāʾobnāyim, and you look upon the birth-stones.
μαιόομαι, to deliver: Middle Liddell's one translation, plain text. Subjunctive after ὅταν, spelled as the indicative, as Koine spells the subjunctive of -όω verbs.
Present middle of περιποιέω: keep for yourselves, preserve. The Hebrew has wāḥāyâ, she shall live.

greek: ἐφοβήθησαν δὲ αἱ μαῖαι τὸν θεὸν καὶ οὐκ ἐποίησαν καθότι συνέταξεν αὐταῖς ὁ βασιλεὺς Αἰγύπτου, καὶ ἐζωογόνουν τὰ ἄρσενα.
hint: The midwives fear God and do not obey the king, but keep the male children alive.

notes.text: ζωογονέω, to engender life, and as ζωγρέω, to keep alive: not in Middle Liddell; LSJ cites this verse for to preserve alive.

greek: ἐκάλεσεν δὲ ὁ βασιλεὺς Αἰγύπτου τὰς μαίας καὶ εἶπεν αὐταῖς Τί ὅτι ἐποιήσατε τὸ πρᾶγμα τοῦτο καὶ ἐζωογονεῖτε τὰ ἄρσενα;
hint: The king calls the midwives and asks why they have done this and let the boys live.

notes.text: Why is it that: τί, the accusative used as an adverb, as at Genesis 18:13.

greek: εἶπαν δὲ αἱ μαῖαι τῷ Φαραω Οὐχ ὡς γυναῖκες Αἰγύπτου αἱ Εβραῖαι, τίκτουσιν γὰρ πρὶν ἢ εἰσελθεῖν πρὸς αὐτὰς τὰς μαίας· καὶ ἔτικτον.
hint: The midwives tell Pharaoh that Hebrew women are not like Egyptian women: they give birth before a midwife arrives.

notes.text: For they bear: the Hebrew first says kî-ḥāyôt hēnnâ, for they are lively, which the Greek has not.
πρὶν ἤ with the infinitive and its subject in the accusative, τὰς μαίας: before the midwives come in.

greek: εὖ δὲ ἐποίει ὁ θεὸς ταῖς μαίαις, καὶ ἐπλήθυνεν ὁ λαὸς καὶ ἴσχυεν σφόδρα.
hint: God deals well with the midwives, and the people grow numerous and very strong.

notes.text: Was doing well to: εὖ ποιέω with the dative, to benefit.

hint: Because the midwives fear God, they make households for themselves.

notes.text: They made households for themselves: the Hebrew has wayyaʿaś lāhem bāttîm, he made them houses, God the subject.

greek: συνέταξεν δὲ Φαραω παντὶ τῷ λαῷ αὐτοῦ λέγων Πᾶν ἄρσεν, ὃ ἐὰν τεχθῇ τοῖς Εβραίοις, εἰς τὸν ποταμὸν ῥίψατε· καὶ πᾶν θῆλυ, ζωογονεῖτε αὐτό.
hint: Pharaoh commands all his people to throw every Hebrew boy into the river and keep every girl alive.

notes.text: To the Hebrews: not in the Hebrew, which has kol-habbēn hayyillôd, every son that is born.
A hanging nominative taken up by αὐτό: every female, keep it alive.
